coverage_estimate: 5,118 of 5,479 readings = 93.4%, measured by exact lowercase string match of every alias against observed_terms.json (200 canonical entries, 1,815 aliases, zero aliases claimed twice — verified by script). The residue is 361 readings across 325 distinct strings, of which 319 strings occur 1-2 times: the tail is one-off wordings and non-types, not a missing subject. Water/sewage process + drinking-water chemistry accounts for ~78% of covered readings, which reflects the sample (20 of 25 collections are municipal water and sewage reports), not the archive.
deliberately_kept_apart: bod (concentration) / bod removal (removal) / bod exceedance frequency (frequency) / bod loading (loading) — four entries on one substance. The removal-vs-frequency pair is the error already published once (Brantford 1962, 'exceeded only 20 per cent of the time' charted as 20% removal); loading is lbs/day applied, not mg/L present.
suspended solids / ss removal / ss exceedance frequency / ss loading — same four-way split, same reasons.

suspended solids vs mixed liquor suspended solids — MLSS runs 1,500-4,000 mg/L inside the aeration tank, effluent SS 10-30 mg/L. Merging draws a monthly two-order-of-magnitude sawtooth that looks like a plant failing and recovering.
capacity (rating, mgd) / flow exceedance frequency (occasions over the rating) / capacity utilisation (per cent of the rating). All three are said with the word 'capacity' and only one is a capacity.
design flow (flow|capacity, a design figure) vs flow (flow|rate, an observation). parameters.py already forces design/rated to measure=capacity; keeping them apart is that rule, not a new one.
total flow (flow|total, a year's volume) vs flow (flow|rate, a daily rate). Named in parameters.py's docstring as the original merge failure.
capacity (plant, mgd) / pump capacity (gpm) / blower capacity (cfm) / chlorinator capacity (lbs per day) / transformer capacity (kVA). Same word, five incompatible axes.

guideline (a published limit) vs the substance's own concentration entry. A guideline charted as a reading is a suspiciously flat line that looks like excellent water; a detection limit charted as a reading is a suspiciously low one.

detection limit (a property of the METHOD) vs guideline (a property of the STANDARD) vs concentration (a property of the WATER). Three different things, all in mg/L, all written about the same substance.

guideline exceedance frequency (a count of occasions) vs guideline exceedance duration (hours the limit stayed passed). Only 1 reading of the second, kept anyway — occasions and hours must never share a key.

labour hours (labour|duration, total effort in man hours) vs staff coverage (staff coverage|rate, hours per day the works is attended). Water aliased these together; 8 hours/day and 1,400 man hours/year are different measurements and neither derives from the other.
staff (headcount on strength, a stock) vs staff hired (arrivals in the year, a flow). Merging puts 2 hires beside 14 on strength.
inspections (visits made) vs equipment inspected (boilers/tanks/cylinders counted) vs deficiencies (findings raised). One inspection can raise several deficiencies.
admissions vs overnight stays — one person is one admission and thirty stays.
efficiency per admission vs efficiency per overnight stay — health merged them; kept apart on the project's own denominator rule (see the cost-per-X entries).

unit cost of treatment ($/million gallons) vs cost per pound of BOD removed ($/lb) vs cost per pound of SS removed vs cost per capita vs cost (dollars). All money; four different denominators and one absolute. This is the rule that stops 'CUBIC FEET AIR PER LB BOD REMOVED' recurring in dollar form.

cost (annual operating/treatment) vs construction cost (capital) — orders of magnitude apart, one annual and one once. parameters.py maps both to substance 'cost'; this is the one place the reconciliation extends rather than follows it, because construction cost does not appear in that table at all.
share of operating costs (%) vs the dollar cost entries — same substance, different measure, so it can never join the dollar series.
chlorine dosage (what was added) vs chlorine residual (what survived) vs chlorinator capacity (what the machine is rated for) vs chemicals cost (what it was billed at).

surface settling rate (gal/day/sq ft) vs weir loading (gal/day/ft) vs flow (mgd). Three 'rates', three axes; a three-figure loading beside a seven-figure daily flow is the same class of merge that broke the flow series.
trihalomethanes (the sum) vs chloroform and dichlorobromomethane (species reported in their own columns beside it).
total reduced sulphur (air concentration) vs sulphate (a dissolved ion in drinking water). Only sulphur-bearing pair in the file and they are not related.
threshold odour and threshold taste — companion tests in adjacent columns, not one test. Neither is a guideline despite the word 'threshold'.

crop yield (spring rye, bushels/acre) vs the sewage 'yield' strings from brantford and kitchener (sludge/vacuum-filter yield). The bare strings are deliberately left uncovered rather than merged into the crop term.
motor power (hp) vs motor speed (rpm) vs voltage (volts) vs power cost (dollars). Four numbers about the same machinery, no two on one axis.
temperature (an observation of water or sludge) vs melting point / boiling point (physical constants of a named compound). Same units, and the second is not a reading of any place or time.
merged_entries: water 'sewage treated' (sewage|total) + water 'total flow' (flow|total) -> total flow. Water itself flagged these as the same physical quantity — gallons through the works in a year — separated only because parameters.py resolves the substance from whichever word appears. 'sewage' names the material, not the measurement.

water 'flow increase' (measure 'change') -> flow|rate. parameters.py already has statistic='change' in _STATISTIC; a new measure for it would have created a second flow-rate series keyed on a qualifier. Same treatment for 'operating cost increase', 'capacity increase', 'power cost saving', 'fuel deficit' and every budget-vs-actual difference: they stay on the parent term.
earth-energy 'rotational speed' + water 'motor speed' + transport-works 'rpm' -> motor speed (motor|rate).
earth-energy 'power' (nameplate) + water 'motor power' + transport-works 'motor power' -> motor power (motor|power).
transport-works 'volume' + water 'tank volume' -> tank volume (tank|capacity). One entry, 232 readings.

transport-works 'diameter' + 'depth' + 'width' + 'length' + 'dimensions' + 'spacing' + 'particle size' + water 'dimension' -> one 'dimension' entry (dimension|length), honouring parameters.py's existing ('diameter'|'width'|'depth' -> 'dimension'). Flagged below: transport-works' argument for splitting the axes is good and this is the entry most likely to need revisiting.
health 'standard plate count' (three entries: count, guideline, frequency) -> one count entry plus the central guideline and guideline-exceedance-frequency entries.
air 'total reduced sulphur exceedance' -> the central guideline exceedance frequency entry (substance carried in the substance field).
education-social 'supervision' + population-economy 'staff coverage' + water's staffing strings -> staff coverage (staff coverage|rate).
education-social 'expenditure' + population-economy 'expenditure' -> one entry; per-capita expenditure strings moved to cost per capita (a ratio, not a sum).
education-social 'assessment' with proposed new measure 'value' -> assessment|cost. A new money measure for 5 readings was not justified; substance keeps it off the payroll axis.
land-resources 'injury zone' + health 'injury zone' -> one entry.
water 'chlorinator capacity' + transport-works' chlorination-capacity aliases -> one entry.
water 'guideline exceedance frequency' + health's 'health related guideline exceedance' + land-resources' 'samples containing more than 9 mg' -> one entry.
collisions_resolved: "temperature" (46 bare + medium-scoped variants): claimed by water and air-emissions. Awarded to water|temperature — parameters.py already has ('temperature','temperature'), and the collections (belleville, brantford, canadianagriculturallibrary, fort-frances) are sewage, sludge and food-storage, not meteorology. Air's own note conceded this. Air's 'storage temperature'/'drying temperature' folded in as aliases rather than left as a second entry.

"motor power"/"horsepower"/"hp" (79 readings): claimed three times — water (substance 'motor'), earth-energy (substance 'power'), transport-works (substance 'motor power'). Awarded to substance 'motor', measure 'power'. Substance 'power' was rejected because earth-energy also uses substance 'power' for the electricity bill; motor|power vs power|cost would then be one substance holding horsepower and dollars.
"rpm"/"motor speed" (26): water, earth-energy and transport-works all proposed it. One entry, motor|rate. Safe alongside motor|power precisely because the measure differs.

"inspections" cluster (25): claimed by health, education-social, earth-energy and transport-works. Awarded to one administration entry. Earth-energy's split was adopted: 'inspections' (acts) kept apart from 'equipment inspected' (boilers, tanks, cylinders, air receivers, moulds, pipe lines — a count of objects). The other three domains merged those and would have put items and visits in one series.
"deficiencies", "audits": claimed by health, education-social and earth-energy. One entry each, administration.

"staff count"/"staff complement"/"men employed": water, education-social and population-economy. One entry, staff|count. 'operators', 'chief operator count' and 'employment' folded in as job-class qualifiers rather than three near-duplicate headcount series.
"man hours" family: water, education-social and population-economy. One entry, labour|duration, matching parameters.py's existing ('man hours' -> 'labour').

"staffing hours per day"/"supervision hours per day": water aliased these into its 'man hours' entry; education-social and population-economy kept them separate. Split upheld — see deliberately_kept_apart.
"salary of j. craig (old)" etc.: education-social and population-economy. One salary|cost entry; the person is the subject and (old)/(new) is the era.
"ascorbic acid" (15): health and land-resources. One entry, food domain, concentration.

"standard plate count" (17): water and health, and health also proposed splitting it three ways. One count entry; its 'limit'/'maximum desirable concentration' strings went to the central guideline entry and its exceedance string to guideline exceedance frequency, so the substance appears once per measure and every alias exactly once.
"bacteriology scan", "aeromonas ... detection frequency": water and health. One entry each, drinking water.
"incubation period" (3): health and land-resources. One entry, food domain (the gerstein collection also holds brine, paprika and egg-laying — laboratory culture, not disease).
"treatment admissions", "overnight stays", "efficiency per ...": health and education-social. One entry each, health.
"injury zone area" (4): health, land-resources and transport-works all touched it. Awarded to air (fort-frances pulp-mill deposition study), measure area.

"<substance> guideline" / "<substance> detection limit" strings: air had 'trs guideline' and 'trs air quality objective' under TRS concentration, health had 'standard plate count limit' under a spc|guideline entry, water had all of them under one central entry. Awarded to the central guideline and detection-limit entries — the measure carries the kind of number and the substance travels in the substance field. This alone de-duplicated ~200 strings that would otherwise have become 60+ junk canonical terms.

"capacity exceedance frequency" (19) and "design flow exceedance frequency" (18): water filed the first under flow|frequency, transport-works filed it under capacity|frequency while leaving the second to water — which would have split ONE measurement across two keys. Merged into flow|frequency; the flow is what exceeded.

"flow as percent of design capacity"/"design capacity percentage": water listed these as aliases of 'design flow' (flow|capacity, a figure in mgd). Removed from there and given their own capacity|ratio entry — a percentage cannot share a series with a rating in million gallons per day.

Bare "volume" (46) and "total volume" (16): water assigned both to tank volume, transport-works assigned bare 'volume' to structure volume and read 'total volume' as throughput. Both assigned to tank|capacity, flagged for human confirmation.

"cost of contract a/b", "total cost stage i": water rejected these as facts, transport-works and population-economy typed them. Kept, under construction cost, with the contract letter and stage read as scope.
"cost to industry of suspensions": earth-energy, health and population-economy all touched it; filed once under cost.

"heat exchanger capacity"/"sludge heater capacity"/"heater rating": only water claimed them; kept in blower capacity (air/thermal equipment) rather than plant capacity so cfm and BTU ratings never join mgd.
dropped_as_facts: cost of converting one boiler plus installing all of the rdf handling and storage systems at the j clark keith station — one boiler, one station, one year; rejected by five domains and correctly so.

cost for construction of pirn street pumping station and clark creek pumping station; interceptor sewer on ontario st. cost; doon primary plant enlargements cost — kept ONLY as aliases of construction cost, never as terms of their own; the named work is the asset, not the measurement type.
sewer baker st; water connection; water and sewer improvement projects — a place, not a quantity.

contract for construction of tug completed; one tug completed; steel tug completed; contract for changes and alteration in tug completed; repairs to curlew; repairs to curleiv — four strings about one vessel plus its OCR twin; completion status, not a number.
count (9 readings, the largest single dropped string) — says what kind of number without saying of what; unusable as a series.
cubic feet (3); treated (3); water (2); raw sewage (2); tanks; water heaters; bacteriological (2); board; ambient — units, materials and bare table headings extracted into the parameter slot.

water quality (5); pesticides impact; specific pesticides; infiltration problem (2); plant operation status; achievable quality rating (2) — name a subject or a state, not a quantity; no measure can be assigned so none can ever be plotted.
measurement range (2) — a property of an instrument; 'range' is already a statistic in parameters.py.
average sewage strength multiplier (2) — a factor used in one calculation in one report.

58 club licenses issued during the year; official delegations from over 50 countries; voluntary sector representatives on the steering committee for the ontario voluntary forum; concurrent working sessions; bulletins mailed on budget night; nations involved — the count is baked into the name, or the string describes one event.
number of tiles or traps used for the first swarm; number of items to be taken; sets of items purchased — counts for one occasion, OCR-damaged, no cluster to anchor to.

drawings and specifications surveyed registered and re registered; designs surveyed and returned to manufacturers for corrections; purchase orders processed by head office staff — three administrative acts fused by a table stub.

subvention applicable la jonction de saint raymond — the only French transport string in the file, and it is a subsidy for one named junction. (Note: French is effectively absent — 3 strings in 2,135 — so this vocabulary has no French aliases yet. That is a gap in the sample, not evidence the corpus is monolingual.)

summer savings; summer saving; of inflation; value of money; income over remitted; market of bonds and stocks over book; sense seeeeteies; nh-f — too vague or too OCR-damaged to assign a substance without guessing.
distance of control locations from pulp mills — kept only as an alias of 'distance'; on its own it describes how one study was laid out.

paprika; brine; spent caustic; wine pulp volume — materials named without a measurement (land-resources proposed paprika and brine as entries; dropped, since the number beside them is a mass in one recipe).
clear wells; screen & surge well; dry well floodings (3) — 'well' in the water-plant sense; must not seed the groundwater-well count.
sunshine (1) — sits in a collection whose neighbours are 'investment' and 'pension expense'; almost certainly a mis-extraction.

days above guideline / percent of days above guideline — KEPT, but only inside the substance-less guideline exceedance frequency entry, where the substance must come from the sentence; they are not entries of their own.
biggest_gaps: count — 9 readings, the largest uncovered string. Deliberately uncovered: it names a measure with no substance. Worth fixing upstream in the extractor, not here.
water quality — 5 readings (brantford, trenton). Names a subject; the extractor is putting a section heading in the parameter slot.

drawback — 4 readings, customs/tax sense, from a sessional-paper revenue table. A real recurring fiscal term that no domain proposed; needs someone who knows the series to say whether it is a refund amount or a count.
treated — 3 readings. A sentence fragment; the substance was lost during extraction.
dry well floodings — 3 readings. A count of flooding events in a pump station; a genuine type with no cluster behind it yet.
cubic feet — 3 readings. The unit landed in the parameter slot.

yield / average yield — 3 readings across brantford and kitchener, meaning sludge or vacuum-filter yield. Left uncovered on purpose: merging them into the crop-yield entry would put bushels per acre and sludge yield in one series, and neither the crop nor the sludge fraction has anywhere to live in substance+measure+statistic+scope.

pressure (2), liabilities (2), cash on hand (2), book of bonds (2), earnings per mile per annum (2), bypass threshold (2), contract for building (2) — the whole remaining tail is 1-2 readings each. 319 of the 325 uncovered strings occur twice or less, so the residue is wording variance and non-types, not a missing subject area.

STRUCTURAL GAP, not a string: the unit of the works has nowhere to live. Roughly 300 readings collapse into 'dimension', 'tank volume', 'retention time', 'area' and 'tank count' only because 'aeration tank', 'primary digester', 'chlorine contact chamber' and 'grit chamber' are treated as qualifiers — but `scope` only accepts primary/secondary/tertiary and cannot express them. A `unit` field is needed or these five entries silently pool distinct vessels.

STRUCTURAL GAP: crop and species have nowhere to live either. 'spring rye yield' loses 'spring rye' entirely; rye and wheat yields would share one key. The same will hit forestry and fisheries the moment those documents are sampled.

STRUCTURAL GAP: budget / actual / forecast / estimate is a qualifier the project has no field for. _STATISTIC covers minimum/maximum/change/range only. Roughly 90 finance readings currently merge a budgeted figure with what was actually spent.

SAMPLE GAP: air, health, education, agriculture, transport, mining and energy are each worth under 2% of readings here because 20 of 25 sampled collections are municipal water and sewage reports. parameters.py's entire air block ('sulphur dioxide', 'ozone', 'dustfall', 'smoke', 'acid precipitation', ...) has ZERO hits in the 2,135 observed strings, while 'total reduced sulphur', which the archive genuinely uses, is missing from it. Those blocks are currently invented vocabulary of exactly the kind this exercise exists to replace, and should be re-derived from a sample that actually contains those subjects.
for_a_human_to_confirm: The 'dimension' entry (370 readings, the second largest in the vocabulary) follows parameters.py in merging diameter, depth, width and length into one substance at measure=length. Transport-works argued for splitting them, and the argument is strong: a clarifier's 85-foot diameter and its 8-foot side-wall depth are both in feet and currently share the key dimension|length. I did not split it because the brief says not to contradict the existing table where it has an answer. This is the single call most likely to be wrong.

Bare 'volume' (46) and 'total volume' (16) are both assigned to tank|capacity. If they are in fact throughput, 62 readings belong in flow|total instead. Two or three source pages would settle it; this is the highest-value manual check in the whole exercise.

Five measure names are new: loading (gal/day/sq ft, lbs/day/cu ft — deliberately not 'rate'), power (horsepower — needed so motor|rate does not hold both hp and rpm), voltage (14 readings, thinnest of the five, added on the precedent that 'temperature' is already its own measure), guideline (209 readings) and detection limit (70). 'change' and 'value' were REJECTED: change duplicates parameters.py's statistic='change', and value collapses into cost. Confirm the five.

'guideline', 'detection limit' and 'guideline exceedance frequency' carry substance = '(the substance named in the string)'. That does not fit the one-substance-per-entry shape of the table. The clean implementation is a measure-detector in resolve() that fires before the substance lookup, in the same position as _FREQUENCY. Without it, 357 readings have no home.

'construction cost' (57) is split from 'cost' (121), which parameters.py does not do. Justification: capital vs annual operating differ by orders of magnitude and construction cost is absent from the existing table, so this extends rather than contradicts. If you would rather not split, collapse it back and the coverage is unchanged.

Contract awards and stage totals ('cost of contract a', 'total cost stage i') are typed as construction cost. The water domain rejected them as facts. I read the contract letter and stage as scope, the way a plant section is.
'equipment cost' pools a $12 bench grinder with a $40,000 vacuum filter (37 readings). Alternative is to flag single-object purchases as unresolved.

Named individuals' salaries ('salary of j. craig (old)') are resolved to salary|cost. Confirm that publishing 1960s named salaries alongside the scanned page is acceptable, or resolve-but-do-not-surface.

'inspections' vs 'equipment inspected' was split following earth-energy; the other three domains merged them. If 'used boilers inspected' really counts inspections rather than boilers, merge — but then the equipment class needs to become a scope.

Physical constants (melting point, boiling point, vapour pressure, Henry's law constant, specific gravity, solubility in water — 41 readings) are included as chemistry entries. They recur per compound, but they are properties of a substance, not observations of a place and time; publishing them beside a scanned page as if they were readings misrepresents them. Include, or exclude all six including solubility?

'trichloroethylene' and '1,1 dichloroethane' are folded into the 'trichloroethane' entry (6 readings) because they appear as one DWSP column family. They are chemically distinct compounds. Split, or leave?

'treatment efficiency' / 'expected efficiency' / 'removal efficiency' (11 readings) are given their own substance 'treatment' rather than being read as BOD removal. In a sewage annual report they almost certainly ARE BOD removal, but the string does not say so — and health's 'efficiency per admission' proves the word alone is not safe.

'lbs boo. per 100 lbs. fti l.s.' (8) is OCR of 'lbs BOD per 100 lbs MLSS', the food-to-microorganism ratio. Filed under bod|loading; strictly it is a mass ratio and may deserve measure=ratio like the air-per-pound-of-BOD entry.

'capacity exceedance frequency' is filed under flow|frequency, not capacity|frequency — the number counts how often the FLOW exceeded the rating. It is the largest string in that cluster (19 readings) and merges with 'design flow exceedance frequency' (18) only under this reading.

'health related and aesthetic objectives' and 'health guidelines' are filed as guidelines. Health read them as a COUNT of how many objectives are health-based. If health is right they move to a count entry; the alias must not appear in both.
